newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-HIRASE LEADS BY ONE SHOT AT LPGA TOUR CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-HIRASE LEADS BY ONE SHOT AT LPGA TOUR CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: Mayumi Hirase of Japan fired a five-under-par 67 Thursday to grab a one-stroke lead over four golfers after the opening round of the inaugural $700,000 LPGA Tour Championship.
Americans Michelle McGann, Jane Geddes, Juli Inkster and Penny Hammel shot 68 in the opening round of the season-ending tournament, which features the top 30 money-earners on the women's U.S. tour.

Sensational Australian newcomer Karrie Webb and British veteran Laura Davies -- locked in a heated battle for the money title with Davies ahead by $45,302 at $897,302 -- were in another group of four players just two strokes behind at 69.

Hirase had three successive birdies on the back nine, including a two-putt from 24 feet on the 15th hole that gave her sole possession of the lead. Hirase also had birdies on the first, third, eighth, 11th, 13th and 14th holes, offsetting bogeys at holes two and six.
"I made a lot of good putts today," said Hirase, who now lives in Irving, Texas, and is a Dallas Cowboys fan.
"When I turned pro in Japan, I wanted to come here and play. I wasn't good enough -- I didn't think I was good enough. This is the best in the world here."
Hirase, 27, has been obscured all year by the 21-year-old Webb, who has 14 top-10 finishes and is certain to win the LPGA Rookie of the Year award.
But Hirase is 17th on the money list with nearly $300,000 and is coming off a playoff win over Davies at the Japan Queens Cup three weeks ago.
"Learning the language has been the toughest part," Hirase said. "I think I'm getting used to it. It's a lot better now."
Hirase, a member of the Japan LPGA since 1988, is 918 points behind Webb in the Rookie of the Year standings.

Davies, 33, has already clinched the 1996 Player of the Year Award. If either Davies or Webb collects the $150,000 first prize here, it will mark the first time an LPGA player has earned more than $1 million in a single season.
